security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans and fixed relative documentation links. One command template passes an unquoted ad-set value to a shell command, and the save template incorporates an ad-set value into a file path. These two instructions require input validation and safe argument handling before use.

remediation.issue: The ledger command places the user-supplied ad-set value in an unquoted shell position.
remediation.suggestion: Use a structured tool call or pass the ad-set as a separately quoted argument after rejecting shell metacharacters and option-like values.

remediation.issue: The save filename includes an ad-set value without a stated filename validation rule.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize the ad-set to a safe filename, reject path separators and traversal segments, then verify the resolved path remains under the memory directory.

content.user_title: Detect Paid Ad Fatigue Before It Wastes Spend
content.value_statement: Scaling campaigns can lose efficiency when repeated exposure weakens response. This skill compares frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach trends to recommend rotating creative, widening audiences, or holding.
actual_capabilities: Compares current frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach against an early-flight baseline.
Distinguishes creative fatigue from audience saturation using reach and frequency trends.
Returns one Rotate-creative, Widen-audience, or Hold trigger for each ad set.
Names the threshold and evidence supporting each trigger.
Flags conversion tracking concerns before using CVR changes for a decision.
limitations: Requires a daily or weekly time series; a single-day snapshot is insufficient.
Cannot assess stable decay while an ad set remains in the learning phase.
Does not create replacement ads or calculate the account RQS score.
Audience saturation may remain estimated when audience-size data is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Scaling Fatigue
use_cases.description: Compare recent ad-set trends with the early-flight baseline and decide whether to rotate creative.

use_cases.title: Separate Saturation From Creative Decay
use_cases.description: Use reach and frequency trends to decide whether a larger audience is needed.

use_cases.title: Validate Conversion Declines
use_cases.description: Compare platform CVR with analytics or commerce records before recommending a campaign change.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Ad Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this daily ad-set export. Compare current frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach with the first stable post-learning window. Return one trigger per ad set.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single advertising set

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Decay Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose whether Ad Set A shows creative fatigue, audience saturation, or normal variation. Explain the observed trends and label every figure by evidence source.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Campaign Segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these prospecting and retargeting sets. Apply objective-specific frequency ceilings, compare decay slopes, and identify the dominant driver when fatigue and saturation coexist.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Measurement Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this campaign trend with GA4 and store conversion data. Check tracking integrity, separate observed decay from inferred causes, and prepare a handoff summary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis with independent conversion evidence

output_examples.input: Frequency rose from 2.1 to 5.8 while CTR fell 38%, CVR stayed stable, and reach continued growing.
output: Evidence: Frequency increased, CTR declined, and reach continued growing.

output_examples.input: Reach plateaued, frequency climbed from 3.4 to 7.1, and both CTR and CVR declined.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: Audience saturation. Trigger: Widen the audience. Reach stopped growing while repeated exposure and response decay increased.

output_examples.input: Platform CVR fell 45%, but order exports remained stable and duplicate conversions appeared in platform reporting.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: Measurement risk. Trigger: Hold. Validate conversion tracking before acting on the reported CVR decline.

best_practices: Provide daily or weekly metrics from the first stable post-learning period through the current date.
Use objective-specific frequency ceilings and state each threshold in the result.
Confirm platform CVR changes with analytics or commerce records whenever possible.
anti_patterns: Do not infer fatigue from one day of data or a single dashboard headline.
Do not apply one universal frequency threshold to every campaign objective.
Do not treat an estimated cause as measured evidence.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide impressions, reach, frequency, clicks or CTR, conversions or CVR, and spend across a daily or weekly time series.

faq.question: Does it require an advertising platform API?
faq.answer: No. Manual exports are sufficient, while keyed platform integrations remain optional.

faq.question: What happens when CVR data is missing?
faq.answer: The skill can assess a creative-fatigue signal from CTR and frequency, but it will mark CVR as unavailable.

faq.question: Can it create replacement advertisements?
faq.answer: No. It diagnoses the trigger and routes creative production to a separate skill.

faq.question: How does it distinguish fatigue from saturation?
faq.answer: Growing reach with declining CTR suggests creative fatigue. Plateaued reach with rising frequency suggests audience saturation.

faq.question: Can the analysis be saved?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks for confirmation before writing a reusable summary to its designated memory directory.
